1.explanation:
• BpmnCopyPaste.copyProperties/removeProperties and its pasteElement handler only copy a small whitelist of properties (name, isExpanded, DI styling) and explicitly strip out oldBusinessObject, so any custom Extension Elements (where async continuation and job config live) are never carried over.  
• ModdleCopy.copyElement governs which moddle properties get deep-copied, and by default disallows certain properties or stops empty Extension Elements from being set. It never adds back any async- or job-related Extension Elements after the boundary conversion.  
• CreateBoundaryEventBehavior’s shape.create interceptor builds a fresh bpmn:BoundaryEvent businessObject with only cancelActivity and attachedToRef set – it never merges or copies any of the source event’s Extension Elements.  
• AttachEventBehavior’s elements.move interceptor does a similar replace via bpmnReplace.replaceElement, only preserving the eventDefinitionType, again dropping all user-configured extensions.  
Together, these handlers are responsible for converting an Intermediate Event into a Boundary Event but neglect to carry over or re-apply any async/job configuration stored in Extension Elements, causing the pasted boundary event to lose all those custom properties.
1.bug_scenario: When a user copies an Intermediate Throw/Catch Event that has Async Continuations or Job Configuration (stored on its Extension Elements) and pastes it onto a Task to become a Boundary Event, all of the previously configured properties disappear. The provided GIF shows an intermediate event with Job Priority set, copied and pasted as a boundary event onto a task, and the pasted boundary event’s property panel no longer shows any of the job or async configuration.

2.explanation: Both CreateBoundaryEventBehavior and AttachEventBehavior intercept the creation or move of an Intermediate Event onto a host and unconditionally create a fresh BoundaryEvent business object with only a minimal set of attributes (cancelActivity, attachedToRef, eventDefinitionType). They never propagate the original element’s extensionElements (where Camunda async/job properties live). On top of that, the BpmnCopyPaste pasteElement handler only copies name and a few DI attributes onto a newly created businessObject of the same type, without explicitly preserving extensionElements. Together, these behaviors strip out all custom Camunda properties when converting an Intermediate Event into a Boundary Event during copy–paste.
2.bug_scenario: When a user copies an Intermediate Event that has custom Camunda properties (e.g. Async Continuations, Job Configuration) and then pastes it onto a Task as a Boundary Event, the pasted Boundary Event loses all of those previously configured properties. In the GIF one sees an Intermediate Event with Job Priority set, copied and then dropped on a Task; the new Boundary Event appears but its Job Priority and other extension fields are empty.
